facts.text: Core Scientific ( NASDAQ:CORZ ) reported third-quarter results on November 5, 2026.

On the earnings call, CEO Adam Sullivan set a date for leaving the Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) business: "We expect to complete our exit from Bitcoin mining by year-end." CFO Jim Nygaard said the company should enter 2027 as a pure-play colocation provider, which means it will only rent data center space and power to AI customers.
Every megawatt billed at Core Scientific is rented by CoreWeave ( NASDAQ:CRWV ).
Core Scientific says the billing capacity equals more than $700 million of annualized colocation revenue.
The revenue mix shows how far the shift has already gone.
Colocation brought in $215.4 million of total revenue of $232.9 million.
That works out to about 92%, up from 83.2% in the second quarter and 18.4% a year earlier.
Self-mining revenue fell to $12.3 million from $57.4 million.
Mining income rises and falls with bitcoin's price and with network difficulty, which measures how hard it is to earn new coins.

Core Scientific carries about $4.3 billion of long-term debt, so delivery delays would hit shareholders first.
If Pecos misses that date, Core Scientific would likely remain dependent on one tenant longer, weakening the case for diversification.
